pr.title: Carry agents' messages between machines through sealed refs in a shared repository
pr.head: c10d7d0b6b9bf948d5f917f820ce99973f6dd3d1

summary: Projector's watch daemon wakes idle Claude Code and Codex sessions with event lines. The layer below this one, agent-messages-local, lets sessions on one machine register under a name and send each other messages through that same delivery. This pull request adds the relay, so sessions on two of your machines can reach each other through a GitHub repository both machines work in. It is the last layer of the agent-messages plan, so it also marks the plan completed.

1. One key opts you in. project agent key init makes an X25519 key pair and stores the private key in the OS keychain, or inline in ~/.projector.toml where there is none. You copy it to your other machines with key export and key import, which run only at a terminal.
  2. Every record is sealed. A session's presence and each message are encrypted and authenticated to the key itself, so the repository holds only ciphertext under random ref names.
  3. Commands queue, the daemon pushes. register and send add a ref change to a per-repository outbox and return at once. The daemon runs one job per repository on worker threads: it fetches the key's refs, opens and checks new records, delivers messages, renews leases, cleans up, and pushes every queued change in one git push.

Two rounds of review fixed three problems in the daemon's job, in relay.py. A planted ref that nests JSON too deeply is now rejected instead of stopping the relay. A message queued while a push runs now goes out on the next tick instead of waiting for the next poll. The check of nesting depth is now a single pass over the bytes, so no planted blob can make it slow. A relayed message's from_machine must also be the machine UUID. No review finding is open. The two-machine check by hand, and the Windows keychain on a real Windows machine, remain for after merge.

cards.title: Terms used on this page
cards.html:
• Presence: a session's sealed registration, at refs/projector/agents/<key-id>/<relay-id>, with a one-hour lease.
  • Relay ID: 16 random hex digits that name a session in ref names instead of its session ID.
  • Outbox: outbox/<owner>/<repo>.json under the watch state root, the ref changes waiting for a push, at most one per ref.
  • Job: one pass of the relay over one repository, run on a worker thread.
  • Lease: --force-with-lease=<ref>:<old>, which makes a push to a moved ref fail when the ref is no longer at the commit the outbox expects.

cards.title: What earlier review rounds settled
cards.html:
• Commands write no Git objects. The daemon writes them in the checkout it pushes from, just before the push.
  • The private key never appears in a command's output or arguments that an agent can see.
  • Relay commits carry a fixed identity and no signature.
  • Relay Git work runs off the daemon's loop, with timeouts.
  • The daemon bounds the work it does on refs anyone with push access can plant.
  • The authority notice comes before any text the sender chose.

groups.title: Sealing a record
groups.kicker: X25519, ChaCha20, and HKDF in the standard library
intro: Projector takes no runtime dependencies, and Python's standard library has no cipher, so this file implements the three published primitives the relay needs. Each is checked against its RFC's test vector.

seal makes a fresh ephemeral key pair for every record. Two key agreements, one with the ephemeral key and one with the sender's own key, feed HKDF, which yields a cipher key and a MAC key. unseal checks the HMAC tag before it decrypts anything. Because each record gets its own key, ChaCha20 runs under an all-zero nonce.

files.note: The primitives and the sealed record format.

checks.text: The code is not constant-time. Only the local daemon and CLI run it, never a service an attacker can time.

groups.title: Storing the key and keeping it out of output
groups.kicker: The keychain backends, the user-layer-only setting, and redaction
intro: The key's private half is the secret that protects every record the relay has carried, so it must not reach an agent's transcript. keychain.py stores it with tools each system ships: security on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows, and secret-tool on Linux. No backend passes the key as an argument, and every call has a 5-second timeout, because a locked macOS keychain waits for a person.

config.py reads agent.key only from ~/.projector.toml, so a checkout cannot plant a key its author knows, and refuses an inline key in a file other accounts can read. redact replaces an inline key, at or under the key a command prints, with <redacted, key ID …>.

files.note: The three keychain backends, each with store, read, and delete under a timeout.
Adds agent.key, the user-only and secret key sets, redact, and the permission check.

groups.title: The relay's job
groups.kicker: Queue, fetch, open, deliver, renew, clean up, and push
intro: relay.py is the heart of the change. Commands call queue, which keeps at most one item per ref in the repository's outbox, because one push refuses two updates to one ref. The daemon's Relay starts a Job per repository on a pool of two threads. A job fetches the key's refs, opens at most 64 new records and checks each one, delivers messages to sessions on this machine, renews and deletes this machine's refs, and pushes the whole outbox in one git push --porcelain. Before it parses an untrusted blob, parse refuses JSON that nests more than 8 deep, and it treats a RecursionError as a record that does not open. The daemon starts a job without a poll only for a queued change that the last job did not try to push.
core.run_bounded runs every relay Git command and keychain tool in its own process group, and kills the group at its timeout, so a hung pre-push hook dies with its parent.

checks.text: Anyone who can push to the repository can plant refs under the key's ID, which git ls-remote shows. So everything a job reads from a fetched ref is untrusted until its tag checks out.

files.note: The key commands' logic, the outbox, the job, and the daemon's relay state.

checks.text: The review reran its reproduction of a planted sealed.json of 32,000 [. The ref is now rejected and deleted, and a later message is delivered.
The review reran its reproduction of a message sent while a pre-push hook held the push. The message now goes out on the next tick with no poll due.

shallow counts depth in one pass that tracks whether it is inside a string and after a backslash, and parse refuses a blob over 32 KiB first. The review timed it at 0.04, 0.08, 0.15, and 0.30 ms on 4, 8, 16, and 32 KiB of escaped quotes, which is linear. Its reproduction of four planted blobs now stalls another thread for 0.02 s at most, against 3 s before.

files.note: Adds run_bounded, which kills a command's whole process group at its timeout.

groups.title: Wiring the relay into sessions and the daemon
groups.kicker: Register and send through the relay, and run it from the watch daemon
intro: agents.py now queues a session's presence when it registers, lists other machines' agents from the relay's cache, and sends to one of them by sealing the message into the outbox. A relayed message becomes a local one before delivery, through deliver, which writes it once and counts a different message under a delivered ID as a collision.

well_formed and well_formed_presence hold the sender fields of a relayed record to the shapes register gives them, including from_machine, which must be the UUID this_machine writes, because the event line and read print them before the authority notice. watch.py ticks the relay each second and reports it in watch status. Codex's SessionEnd hook starts the daemon so a registered session's refs get deleted.

files.note: Relayed register, list, send, read, and the sender-field checks.
Creates the daemon's Relay, ticks it each second, and keeps the daemon running while a relay job is busy.
Starts the daemon on SessionEnd for a registered session.

groups.title: The key commands and redacted config output
groups.kicker: project agent key, the relay header, and config redaction
intro: cli.py adds project agent key init, show, export, import, and remove. export and import refuse unless standard input and output are a terminal. config set agent.key is refused, and every value config get, list, set, and unset print passes through redact. send prints a reminder when the relayed repository is not private.

files.note: The key subcommands, the relay lines in agent list and watch status, and redaction in the config commands.

groups.title: Documentation, the skill, and the plan
groups.kicker: How agents and people use the relay, and what building it settled
intro: The message-agent skill gains the rules the local layer deferred. An agent never runs the key commands unless asked, and in a public repository a message names no private repository. docs/cli.md documents the key and the relay. The plan records what the relay settled in § 10, its outcome in § 11, and moves to completed.

files.note: Adds leaving the key to the user, finding a peer on another machine, and the public-repository rule.
§ 10 lists what the relay settled, and § 11 records the outcome.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: RFC vectors, and two simulated machines sharing a bare origin
intro: test_relay.py stands up a temporary bare repository and two machines, each with its own home, state root, and checkout, with fake keychain tools that record every call. Each test is named after an acceptance criterion in plan § 4.
